verdicts.evidence: The `if` condition directly calls `os.path.exists` on the stated path (f1:12).
The test is `not os.path.exists(...)`, and the guarded then block runs when that existence test is false (f1:12-14).
The condition checks whether the named filesystem path exists using `os.path.exists` (f1:12).
There is one `if` guard, and its then region is controlled by exactly the single `not_exists` condition (f1:12-14).

On the then side, the code downloads and expands an archive, removes the temporary archive, installs dependencies, and starts the updater (f1:14); these actions are enabled by the missing-directory test.
The installation actions run when the specified updater directory is absent, so the gate activates the actions on that condition (f1:12-14).
The code does not explain why this directory controls installation; it only skips the install command when the directory exists, leaving the gate's purpose unclear (f1:12-14).
The guarded region calls `run(...)` (f1:14), whose definition invokes `subprocess.Popen(...)` (f1:7-9), so the execution sink is reached through the stated call and definition hops on the then side.
The only call to `run` in setup.py is inside the guarded then block, and the `Popen` sink is inside `run` (f1:7-14); no other caller reaches that sink.

The guarded command downloads an archive, writes it to the temporary path and expands it, removes the archive, then starts hidden processes; these support download, file write, deletion, execution, and defense evasion respectively (f1:14).
